thread:
maria: Heads-up — during the last canary we saw a small but reproducible tail when a shard went into degraded GPU mode. It looks like continuous batching kept trying to pack requests for that shard and latency spiraled. Thoughts on practical fallbacks? :frowning:
kevin: ugh. saw that too. was watching traces, the batcher kept waiting 20–30ms for the slow slot and other tenants hit tail.
anjali: do we have per-shard health signals wired into admission? if not, we should gate batching on an LRU health hint.
sam: quick idea: if a shard reports degraded for >2s, switch its routing to a micro-window fastpath (small fixed-size batch) + disable packing for that shard. cheap to implement as a per-shard policy.
maria: agree. need to be careful about starvation — moving to micro-window increases per-token cost for that shard but keeps others fast. tradeoff is cost vs global latency.
kevin: propose a 3-tier fallback: healthy -> conservative pack -> micro-window. transitions based on consecutive p90 violations and a simple cooldown.
anjali: let's define failure domain semantics: degraded = internal GPU queue depth anomalies or >X% decode time variance. we should avoid oscillation. add hysteresis.
sam: add quota buffer too — when we move shard to micro-window, temporarily reduce its enqueue credits so it can't flood. simple token-bucket tweak.
kevin: curious about KV cache warmness when we move routes — could cause extra decode work. we probably need a warmup hint or keep KV pinned for a short TTL while transitioning.
maria: good call. keep a short overlap: route new requests to micro-window, but keep in-flight batches on primary for up to 200ms to preserve KV locality.
anjali: ops-bot: can we add a synthetic metric for "shard-packing-impact" so we can alert when a single shard's packing delay increases system-wide p99?
ops-bot: added metric proposal to infra board, link: https://confluence.internal/infra/shard-packing-impact. will emit p50/p90/p99 per-shard and a cross-shard delta.
sam: also worth documenting queue contracts: producer should be able to annotate request with 'latency_sensitivity' and batcher respects it by opting out of packing. that helps SaaS customers prioritize.
maria: yes — add request-level hints: latency_sensitivity: high/normal, allow_batching: true/false, fallthrough_policy: "route"|"hold". default should be safe.\e kevin: small config sketch:
```
shardFallback:
  thresholds:
    p90_ms: 50
    consecutive: 3
  fallback: micro_window
  cooldown_s: 30
```
kevin: implement as config plus runtime override via console for canaries.
anjali: we need to avoid per-request config explosion. make shard policy evaluate deterministically from health tags + tenant override. console toggle is fine.
maria: ops question — when shard is degraded, should we proactively rebalance tenants away from it? or just failover routing? both have pros/cons.
sam: proactive rebalance is heavy (state movement, KV loss). prefer routing shadow -> warm -> cutover, with a decaying sticky policy so tenants slowly migrate if degradation persists.
kevin: test plan: fuzz shard degrade, ensure no more than 5% increase in other tenants' p99. run with 10k requests/s synthetic with mixed sizes.
anjali: add a simple postmortem template: timeline, root cause, mitigation chosen, cost delta. keep it short.
maria: agree. can someone own the RFC follow-up doc? sam?
sam: i'll draft the follow-up RFC with concrete APIs and a minimal POC (micro-window allocator + shard health hook). aim for next Wed.
maria: thanks. in the meantime, ops-bot, please flag any shard with p90 drift > 1.5x baseline during rollout. :thumbsup: 
ops-bot: will do. alert configured: channel #eng-runtime-alerts and email to eng-runtime-oncall.
kevin: one last thought — consider a debug-only path that force-bypasses packing to reproduce locally without cluster-wide churn. tiny CLI flag on the client.
anjali: +1, helps debugging.
maria: cool. action items: sam RFC, ops add metric/alerts (ops-bot done), kevin add config prototype, anjali add hysteresis rules, everyone add test ideas to the RFC. we'll reconvene after draft.
